_comment: Recorded, checked-in baseline for scripts/validate_all.py to regression-test against. Updated 2026-09-12 after replacing data-pipeline/scripts/generate_synthetic.py's hand-tuned noise (rng.uniform ranges picked to 'look plausible') with a real distribution fit: Ceramics and Textiles now draw from a Gaussian parameterised by a coefficient of variation computed from real BEE/SAMEEEKSHA cluster-manual Specific-Energy-Consumption range tables (Morbi ceramic cluster Table 7, Surat textile cluster Table 5) instead of an arbitrary interval — see generate_synthetic.py's SEC_CV_BY_SECTOR docstring for the full sourcing and the exact CV arithmetic. Chemicals/Engineering had no equally-normalised public source located in this pass and deliberately keep their prior (disclosed, unsourced) noise range unchanged rather than borrowing another sector's number. This first update-baseline run also caught and fixed a real bug before landing: an initial version applied the sourced CV redundantly across three multiplicative noise layers instead of one, which compounded to far more variance than intended and cratered z-score precision to 0.09 — the tolerance floors below caught it, exactly what this file is for. z-score precision moved 0.553->0.49 (still above its 0.45 floor) and benchmark model improvement moved 38.3%/12.9%->30.6%/7.1% (both still above their floors) as a real, understood consequence of Ceramics/Textiles now having genuinely tighter, sourced month-to-month variance than the old blanket assumption. If you regenerate the synthetic dataset or retrain a model, re-run scripts/validate_all.py --update-baseline to intentionally accept new numbers — never hand-edit this file to make a failing check pass.

zscore_anomaly_detector.description: backend/app/intelligence/anomaly.py — the anomaly detector actually in production.
zscore_anomaly_detector.note: Tolerance band, not an exact-match requirement: small ground-truth-label drift from re-running the synthetic generator is expected and fine; a drop below these floors means a real regression (e.g. someone loosened the thresholds) and should block a ship.

benchmark_model.description: ml/benchmark_model.py (LightGBM) vs. the flat sourced benchmark.
benchmark_model.note: min_leave_one_cluster_out_improvement_pct=0.0 means: must not be WORSE than the flat benchmark for a brand-new cluster (that was the original bug this model found and fixed at the data-generator level — see data-pipeline/LIMITATIONS.md #9). Going negative again would mean that fix broke.

symbiosis_matcher.note: min_semantic_similarity_threshold must stay >= the value that excluded the textile_sludge/cotton_waste false-positive match found during Phase 3c (see ml/LIMITATIONS.md) — lowering it silently would reintroduce that exact bug.

anomaly_autoencoder.description: ml/anomaly_model.py (PyTorch) — built, evaluated, intentionally NOT in production.
anomaly_autoencoder.note: This is a sanity check, not a quality bar: if a future retrain suddenly reports 'beats_baseline', that's worth a deliberate human decision to promote it to production — not something that should happen silently via an automated pipeline. Flagged, not failed.

anomaly_ensemble.description: ml/anomaly_ensemble.py — z-score + autoencoder combined (OR/AND/weighted-sum variants), the Phase-4 revisit attempt. Built, evaluated, intentionally NOT in production.
anomaly_ensemble.note: Same sanity-check discipline as anomaly_autoencoder above. The AND variant does beat the production rule on precision alone (0.533 vs 0.49) but not recall (0.615 vs 0.962) — see ml/LIMITATIONS.md for the full breakdown and the two-tier-confidence idea this suggests for future work. Flagged, not failed, if a future run's best variant beats both metrics at once.
